May I be rich in food, an eater of food, svCihd. In my seed rest the waters, seed in the heart, the heart in the self. That is the truth of the deities. I shall not die against m}^ will. May I be rich in food, an eater of food, avail a. In my strength rests Indra, strength in the heart, the heart in the self. That is the truth of the deities. I shall not die against my will. May I be rich in food, an eater of food, srdhd. In my anger rests Isana, anger in the heart, the heart in the self. That is the truth of the deities. I shall not die against my will. May I be rich in food, an eater of food, svd/id. In mj head rests the ether, the head in the heart, the heart in the self. That is the truth of the deities, I shall not die against my will. May I be rich in food, an eater of food, srdhd. In my self rests Brahman(n.), the self in the heart, svd/id,' (he repeats), and sacrifices by consuming the remains of the pot of milk.
11.6.m: ‘Agni is established in my speech; speech in the heart; the heart in the self. That is the truth of the gods. May I not die without my wish; may I possess food, may I be an eater of food, svāhā! Vāyu is established in my breath; breath in the heart; the heart in the self. That is the truth of the gods. May I not die without my wish; may I possess food, may I be an eater of food, svāhā! Lightnings are established in my downward breath; downward breath in the heart; the heart in the self. That is the truth of the gods. May I not die without my wish; may I possess food, may I be an eater of food, svāhā! Parjanya is established in my upward breath; upward breath in the heart; the heart in the self. That is the truth of the gods. May I not die without my wish; may I possess food, may I be an eater of food, svāhā! The sun is established in my eye; the eye in the heart; the heart in the self. That is the truth of the gods. May I not die without my wish; may I possess food, may I be an eater of food, svāhā! The moon is established in my mind; the mind in the heart; the heart in the self. That is the truth of the gods. May I not die without my wish; may I possess food, may I be an eater of food, svāhā! The directions are established in my ear; the directions in the heart; the heart in the self. That is the truth of the gods. May I not die without my wish; may I possess food, may I be an eater of food, svāhā! The earth is established in my body; the earth in the heart; the heart in the self. That is the truth of the gods. May I not die without my wish; may I possess food, may I be an eater of food, svāhā! Indra is established in my strength; strength in the heart; the heart in the self. That is the truth of the gods. May I not die without my wish; may I possess food, may I be an eater of food, svāhā! Īśāna is established in my wrath; wrath in the heart; the heart in the self. That is the truth of the gods. May I not die without my wish; may I possess food, may I be an eater of food, svāhā! Space is established in the crown of my head; the crown of the head in the heart; the heart in the self. That is the truth of the gods. May I not die without my wish; may I possess food, may I be an eater of food, svāhā! Brahman is established in my self; the self in the heart; the heart in the self. That is the truth of the gods. May I not die without my wish; may I possess food, may I be an eater of food, svāhā!’ Then, pouring this remainder of the boiled mess of food onto himself, he makes an offering.

11.7.s: aśmā jāgatam ayas traiṣṭubhaṃ loham auṣṇihaṃ sīsaṃ kākubhaṃ rajataṃ svārājyaṃ suvarṇaṃ gāyatram annaṃ vairājaṃ tṛptir ānuṣṭubhaṃ nākaṃ sāmrājyaṃ bṛhaspatir bārhataṃ brahma pāṅktaṃ prajāpatir ātichandasaṃ sāvitrī sarvavedachandasena chandaseti ||
11.7.d: अश्मा जागतम् अयस् त्रैष्टुभं लोहम् औष्णिहं सीसं काकुभं रजतं स्वाराज्यं सुवर्णं गायत्रम् अन्नं वैराजं तृप्तिर् आनुष्टुभं नाकं साम्राज्यं बृहस्पतिर् बार्हतं ब्रह्म पाङ्क्तं प्रजापतिर् आतिछन्दसं सावित्री सर्ववेदछन्दसेन छन्दसेति ||
11.7.e: Stone is of Jagati, iron of Tristubh, copper of Usnih, lead of Kakubh, silver of Svarilj, gold of Gayatrl, food of Viraj, enjoyment of Anustubh, the firmament of Samrilj, Brhaspati of BrhatT, Brahman(n.) of Pankti, Prajapati of Atichandas, the Savitri of the metre of all the Vedas.
11.7.m: Stone is of the Jagatī metre; iron of the Triṣṭubh; copper of the Uṣṇih; lead of the Kakubh; silver of self-rule; gold of the Gāyatrī; food of the Virāj; satisfaction of the Anuṣṭubh; the firmament of universal rule; Bṛhaspati of the Bṛhatī; Brahman of the Paṅkti; Prajāpati of the hyper-metre; the Sāvitrī of the metres of all the Vedas—thus the metres.

11.8.s: aśmeva sthiro vasāni jāgatena chandasā | puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ sūtram annaṃ granthis taṃ granthim udgrathnāmy annakāmaḥ | mṛtyave brāhmaṇaṃ api sarvam āyur aśīyāyuṣmān māham akāmo mariṣyāmy annavān annādo bhūyāsaṃ svāhā | aya iva sthiro vasāni traiṣṭubhena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ … svāhā | loham iva sthiro vasāny auṣṇihena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ … svāhā | sīsam iva sthiro vasāni kākubhena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ … svāhā | rajatam iva sthiro vasāni svarājyena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ … svāhā | suvarṇam iva sthiro vasāni gāyatreṇa chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ … svāhā | annam iva sthiro vasāni vairājena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ … svāhā | tṛptir iva sthiro vasāny ānuṣṭubhena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ … svāhā | nākam iva sthiro vasāni sāmrājyena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ … svāhā | bṛhaspatir iva sthiro vasāni bārhatena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ … svāhā | brahmeva sthiro vasāni pāṅktena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ … svāhā | prajāpatir iva sthiro vasāny ātichandasena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ … svāhā | sāvitrīr iva sthiro vasāni sarvavedachandasena chandasā puruṣo maṇiḥ prāṇaḥ … svāhā | priyāyai vā jāyāyai priyāya vāntevāsine 'nyasmai vāpi yasmai kāmayeta tasmā ucchiṣṭaṃ dadyāt | sa hāpi śataṃ varṣāṇi jīvati punaḥ punaḥ prayuñjāno jīvaty eva jīvaty eva ||
11.8.d: अश्मेव स्थिरो वसानि जागतेन छन्दसा | पुरुषो मणिः प्राणः सूत्रम् अन्नं ग्रन्थिस् तं ग्रन्थिम् उद्ग्रथ्नाम्य् अन्नकामः | मृत्यवे ब्राह्मणं अपि सर्वम् आयुर् अशीयायुष्मान् माहम् अकामो मरिष्याम्य् अन्नवान् अन्नादो भूयासं स्वाहा | अय इव स्थिरो वसानि त्रैष्टुभेन छन्दसा पुरुषो मणिः प्राणः … स्वाहा | लोहम् इव स्थिरो वसान्य् औष्णिहेन छन्दसा पुरुषो मणिः प्राणः … स्वाहा | सीसम् इव स्थिरो वसानि काकुभेन छन्दसा पुरुषो मणिः प्राणः … स्वाहा | रजतम् इव स्थिरो वसानि स्वराज्येन छन्दसा पुरुषो मणिः प्राणः … स्वाहा | सुवर्णम् इव स्थिरो वसानि गायत्रेण छन्दसा पुरुषो मणिः प्राणः … स्वाहा | अन्नम् इव स्थिरो वसानि वैराजेन छन्दसा पुरुषो मणिः प्राणः … स्वाहा | तृप्तिर् इव स्थिरो वसान्य् आनुष्टुभेन छन्दसा पुरुषो मणिः प्राणः … स्वाहा | नाकम् इव स्थिरो वसानि साम्राज्येन छन्दसा पुरुषो मणिः प्राणः … स्वाहा | बृहस्पतिर् इव स्थिरो वसानि बार्हतेन छन्दसा पुरुषो मणिः प्राणः … स्वाहा | ब्रह्मेव स्थिरो वसानि पाङ्क्तेन छन्दसा पुरुषो मणिः प्राणः … स्वाहा | प्रजापतिर् इव स्थिरो वसान्य् आतिछन्दसेन छन्दसा पुरुषो मणिः प्राणः … स्वाहा | सावित्रीर् इव स्थिरो वसानि सर्ववेदछन्दसेन छन्दसा पुरुषो मणिः प्राणः … स्वाहा | प्रियायै वा जायायै प्रियाय वान्तेवासिने ऽन्यस्मै वापि यस्मै कामयेत तस्मा उच्छिष्टं दद्यात् | स हापि शतं वर्षाणि जीवति पुनः पुनः प्रयुञ्जानो जीवत्य् एव जीवत्य् एव ||
11.8.e: May I be established firm as a stone by the Jagati metre. Man is the jewel, breath the thread, food the knot, that knot I tie, desiring food, a holy power against death. May I obtain full length of days, long lived. I shall not die against my will. May I be rich in food, an eater of food, f>rd/id. 1 i.e. he drinks it. May I be established firm as iron by the Tristubh metre. Man is the jewel,' etc. May I be established firm as copper by the Usnih metre. Man is the jewel, etc. May I be established firm as lead by the Kakubh metre. Man is the jewel, etc. May I be established firm as silver by the Svaraj metre. Man is the jewel, etc. May I be established firm as gold by the Gayatrl metre. Man is the jewel, etc. May I be established firm as food by the Yiraj metre. Man is the jewel, etc. May I be established firm as enjoyment by the Anustubh metre. Man is the jewel, etc. May I be established firm as the firmament by the Samraj - metre. Man is the jewel, etc. May I be established firm as Brhaspati by the BrhatI metre. Man is the jewel, etc. May I be established firm as Brahman(n.) by the Pahkti metre. Man is the jewel, etc. May I be established firm as Prajapati by the Atichandas metre. Man is the jewel, etc. May I be established firm as the Savitrl by the metre of all the Vedas. Man is the jewel,' etc. (he repeats). Either to a dear wife, or a dear pupil, or to whomsoever else he favours, he should give the remains of the oblation. He indeed lives a hundred years, who ever and again performs this (rite).
11.8.m: ‘Firm like stone may I abide, through the Jagatī metre. The person is the jewel, breath the thread, food the knot; that knot I untie, desiring food. [Deliver] the Brahmin from death! May I attain a full lifespan; may I live long; may I not die without my wish; may I possess food, may I be an eater of food, svāhā!’ ‘Firm like iron may I abide, through the Triṣṭubh metre. The person is the jewel, breath... svāhā!’ ‘Firm like copper may I abide, through the Uṣṇih metre. The person is the jewel, breath... svāhā!’ ‘Firm like lead may I abide, through the Kakubh metre. The person is the jewel, breath... svāhā!’ ‘Firm like silver may I abide, through the metre of self-rule. The person is the jewel, breath... svāhā!’ ‘Firm like gold may I abide, through the Gāyatrī metre. The person is the jewel, breath... svāhā!’ ‘Firm like food may I abide, through the Virāj metre. The person is the jewel, breath... svāhā!’ ‘Firm like satisfaction may I abide, through the Anuṣṭubh metre. The person is the jewel, breath... svāhā!’ ‘Firm like the firmament may I abide, through the metre of universal rule. The person is the jewel, breath... svāhā!’ ‘Firm like Bṛhaspati may I abide, through the Bṛhatī metre. The person is the jewel, breath... svāhā!’ ‘Firm like Brahman may I abide, through the Paṅkti metre. The person is the jewel, breath... svāhā!’ ‘Firm like Prajāpati may I abide, through the hyper-metre. The person is the jewel, breath... svāhā!’ ‘Firm like the Sāvitrī [verses] may I abide, through the metre of all the Vedas. The person is the jewel, breath... svāhā!’ He should give the remainder of the food to his beloved wife, or to a beloved resident pupil, or to whomever else he may desire. He indeed lives a hundred years; practicing it again and again, he truly lives, he truly lives.

12.1.s: om | hastivarcasaṃ prathatāṃ bṛhad vayo yad adityai tanvaḥ saṃbabhūva | tan mahyaṃ samaduḥ sarva eta ādityāso adityā saṃvidānāḥ || yat te varco jātavedo bṛhad bhavaty āhitam | tena mā varcasā tvam agne varcasvinaṃ kuru || yac ca varco vā puruṣe yac ca hastiṣv āhitam | suvarṇe goṣu yad varco mayi tad dhastivarcasam || yad akṣeṣu hiraṇyeṣu goṣv aśveṣu yad yaśaḥ | surāyāṃ pūyamānāyāṃ mayi tad dhastivarcasam || mayi bhargo mayi maho mayi yajñasya yad yaśaḥ | tan mayi prajāpatir divi divam iva dṛṃhatu ||
12.1.d: ओम् | हस्तिवर्चसं प्रथतां बृहद् वयो यद् अदित्यै तन्वः संबभूव | तन् मह्यं समदुः सर्व एत आदित्यासो अदित्या संविदानाः || यत् ते वर्चो जातवेदो बृहद् भवत्य् आहितम् | तेन मा वर्चसा त्वम् अग्ने वर्चस्विनं कुरु || यच् च वर्चो वा पुरुषे यच् च हस्तिष्व् आहितम् | सुवर्णे गोषु यद् वर्चो मयि तद् धस्तिवर्चसम् || यद् अक्षेषु हिरण्येषु गोष्व् अश्वेषु यद् यशः | सुरायां पूयमानायां मयि तद् धस्तिवर्चसम् || मयि भर्गो मयि महो मयि यज्ञस्य यद् यशः | तन् मयि प्रजापतिर् दिवि दिवम् इव दृंहतु ||
12.1.e: Om. May that splendour of the elephant, of great power, manifest itself which was born from Aditi's body. That all those have given to me, the Adityas in unison with Aditi. The great splendour that is deposited in thee, Jatavedas, with that splendour do thou make me resplendent.-^ The splendour that is in man, that is deposited in elephants, the splendour in gold and kine, in me be that splendour of the elephant. The glory that there is in golden dice,- in cows and horses, in the Sura being purified, in me be that splendour of the elephant. In me be radiance, in me greatness, in me the glory of the sacrifice, in me may Prajapati make that fast as the heaven in the sky.
12.1.m:
Om. May the elephant's splendour spread abroad, the great vigour which arose from Aditi's body. / That all these Ādityas, in agreement with Aditi, have bestowed upon me. ||1
Whatever great splendour is placed in you, O Jātavedas, / with that splendour, O Agni, make me splendid. ||2
Whatever splendour is placed in man, and whatever in elephants, / whatever splendour is in gold, in cattle—may that elephant's splendour be in me! ||3
Whatever glory is in dice, in gold, in cattle, in horses, / in surā being purified—may that elephant's splendour be in me! ||4
In me be brilliance, in me be greatness, in me whatever glory of the sacrifice! / May Prajāpati firmly establish that in me, as heaven in the sky! ||5

12.2.s: aśvinā sāragheṇa mā sam aṅktāṃ madhunā payaḥ | yathā madhumatīṃ vācam āvadāni janeṣu || ghṛtād ullupto madhumān payasvān dhanaṃjayo dharuṇo dhārayiṣṇuḥ | rujan sapatnān adharāṃś ca kṛṇvan ā roha māṃ mahate saubhagāya || prajāpate na tvad etāny anyo viśvā jatāni pari tā babhūva | yatkāmās te juhumas tan no astu vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇām || ayaṃ sano nudatāṃ me sapatnān indra iva vṛtraṃ pṛtanāsu sāḷhā | agnir iva kakṣaṃ vibhṛtaḥ purutrā vāteṣu nas tigmajambho 'nu mārṣṭi || ayaṃ sano yo 'nuvādī kīla iva vṛtraṃ vi puro ruroja | anenendro vi mṛdho vihatyā śatrūyatām ābharā bhojanāni ||
12.2.d: अश्विना सारघेण मा सम् अङ्क्तां मधुना पयः | यथा मधुमतीं वाचम् आवदानि जनेषु || घृताद् उल्लुप्तो मधुमान् पयस्वान् धनंजयो धरुणो धारयिष्णुः | रुजन् सपत्नान् अधरांश् च कृण्वन् आ रोह मां महते सौभगाय || प्रजापते न त्वद् एतान्य् अन्यो विश्वा जतानि परि ता बभूव | यत्कामास् ते जुहुमस् तन् नो अस्तु वयं स्याम पतयो रयीणाम् || अयं सनो नुदतां मे सपत्नान् इन्द्र इव वृत्रं पृतनासु साऌहा | अग्निर् इव कक्षं विभृतः पुरुत्रा वातेषु नस् तिग्मजम्भो ऽनु मार्ष्टि || अयं सनो यो ऽनुवादी कील इव वृत्रं वि पुरो रुरोज | अनेनेन्द्रो वि मृधो विहत्या शत्रूयताम् आभरा भोजनानि ||
12.2.e: May the Asvins anoint me with the honey of bees, with milk, that a honey-sweet voice I may utter among the folk. Snatched out of ghee, rich in honey and milk, winning wealth, bearing and supporting, destroying our foes and putting them down, mount upon me for great good fortune. None other than thou, Prajapati, doth encircle all these beings. That for which we long in sacrificing to thee, be that ours. May we be lords of riches. May this ancient (amulet) crush my foes, even as Indra Vrtra, enduring in the battles. As Agni a forest, spread widely, so in the winds the sharp-toothed one rubs me.' This ancient one who accords with us in sooth, as Indra Vrtra, has rent the burghs asunder. With this, Indra, smiting aside the foes, bring us the wealth of the hostile ones.'
12.2.m:
May the two Aśvins anoint me with honey gathered by bees, [with] milk, / so that I may speak honeyed speech among the people. ||6
Smeared with clarified butter, full of honey, rich in milk, winning wealth, supporting, sustaining, / breaking rivals and casting them low: mount upon me for great good fortune! ||7
O Prajāpati, no other than you has encompassed all these creatures. / With whatever desire we offer to you, let that be ours; may we be lords of riches! ||8
May this [amulet of] sanapuṣpī thrust away my rivals, as Indra, conquering in battles, [thrust away] Vṛtra; / as Agni, carried abroad in many places, with sharp jaws consumes the brushwood when the winds blow, so may he wipe away our [enemies]! ||9
This [amulet of] sanapuṣpī, which answers like a peg, broke down the strongholds as Indra [broke] Vṛtra; / by this may Indra, having struck down the assailants, bring hither the possessions of those acting as enemies! ||10

12.3.s: jayendra śatrūñ jahi śūra dasyūn vṛtraṃ hatveva kuliśenā vi vṛśca | augha iva śāpān pra ṇudāt sapatnāñ jahyāt sapatnān svadhitir vaneva || anu vṛśca madhyāt prati vṛścopariṣṭād vi vṛśca paścāt prati śūra vṛśca | tvayā praṇuttān maghavann amitrān śūra riṣantaṃ maruto 'nu yantu || tvāṃ rudrair hetibhiḥ pinvamānā indraṃ manvānā maruto juṣanta | suparṇāḥ kaṅkāḥ pra mṛśanto enān mahīyatāṃ daṃṣṭrī vardhaneṣu || brahmaṇuttasya maghavan pṛtanyato viṣvag indra bhaṅgāḥ patantu | mā jñātāram īśata mā pratiṣṭhāṃ mitho vighnānā upa yānti mṛtyum || agne yaśasvin yaśase sam arpayendravatīm apacitim ihā vaha | ayaṃ mūrdhā parameṣṭhī suvarcāḥ sajātānām uttamaśloko astu ||
12.3.d: जयेन्द्र शत्रूञ् जहि शूर दस्यून् वृत्रं हत्वेव कुलिशेना वि वृश्च | औघ इव शापान् प्र णुदात् सपत्नाञ् जह्यात् सपत्नान् स्वधितिर् वनेव || अनु वृश्च मध्यात् प्रति वृश्चोपरिष्टाद् वि वृश्च पश्चात् प्रति शूर वृश्च | त्वया प्रणुत्तान् मघवन्न् अमित्रान् शूर रिषन्तं मरुतो ऽनु यन्तु || त्वां रुद्रैर् हेतिभिः पिन्वमाना इन्द्रं मन्वाना मरुतो जुषन्त | सुपर्णाः कङ्काः प्र मृशन्तो एनान् महीयतां दंष्ट्री वर्धनेषु || ब्रह्मणुत्तस्य मघवन् पृतन्यतो विष्वग् इन्द्र भङ्गाः पतन्तु | मा ज्ञातारम् ईशत मा प्रतिष्ठां मिथो विघ्नाना उप यान्ति मृत्युम् || अग्ने यशस्विन् यशसे सम् अर्पयेन्द्रवतीम् अपचितिम् इहा वह | अयं मूर्धा परमेष्ठी सुवर्चाः सजातानाम् उत्तमश्लोको अस्तु ||
12.3.e: Conquer the foes, conquer, hero, the enemy. Slaying Yrtra, cleave him with thine axe. Like the flood pieces of wood, let him smite away our foes, and lay low our enemies as an axe the woods. Cleave along from the middle, cleave forward from above, cleave from behind, cleave, O hero; the foes smitten by thee, 0 bountiful one, 0 hero, let the Maruts follow thee as thou destroyest. Thee swelling with Rudra's darts, deeming thee Indra, let the Maruts gladly choose. Let the vultures and herons seize on them (the foes). May the tusker be joyous in the increase. 0 bountiful one, may thy blows fall on all sides on the enemy smitten by the spell. May they own no friend, no support. Mutually hindering they go to death. 0 glorious Agni, bring us to glory. Bring hither Indra's recompense. May he be the head, the supreme, the splendid, of his kinsmen may he have the highest praise.
12.3.m:
Conquer, O Indra, the enemies; slay, O hero, the Dasyus; as if having slain Vṛtra, cut them to pieces with the axe! / As a flood [washes away] curses, let it drive away rivals; let it cut down rivals as an axe cuts trees! ||11
Cut them through from the middle, cut them through from above, cut them apart from behind, O hero, cut them down! / The enemies driven off by you, O Maghavan, may the Maruts pursue, harming [them], O hero! ||12
Swell with Rudra-weapons, thinking on Indra, the Maruts took delight in you; / let the fair-winged vultures, tearing them to pieces, exalt the tusked one among the increasers! ||13
Driven by the sacred formula, O Maghavan, let the fragments of him who fights against [us] fall scattered on all sides, O Indra! / May they find no one who knows them, no support; striking one another down, may they go to death! ||14
O glorious Agni, unite [me] with glory; bring hither homage accompanied by Indra! / May this head, supreme, full of splendour, be celebrated with the highest praise among his kinsmen! ||15

12.4.s: bhadraṃ paśyanta upa sedur āgan tato dīkṣām ṛṣayaḥ svarvidaḥ | tataḥ kṣatraṃ balam ojaś ca jātaṃ tad asmai devā abhi saṃ namantām || dhātā vidhātā paramota saṃdṛk prajāpatiḥ parameṣṭhī suvarccāḥ | stomāṃś chandāṃsi nivido ma āhur etasmai rāṣṭram abhi saṃ namantām || abhy ā vartadhvam upa sevatāgnim ayaṃ śāstādhipatir no astu | asya vijñānam anu saṃ rabhadhvam imaṃ paścād anu jīvātha sarve || alardo nāma jāto 'si purā sūryāt puroṣasaḥ | taṃ tvā sapatnakṣayaṇaṃ vedātha viṣṭambhajambhanam || nārdhe pramīyeta tared dviṣantaṃ kalpeta vākyaṃ pṛtanāḥ saheta | pramāyukaṃ tasya dviṣantam āhur irāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti ||
12.4.d: भद्रं पश्यन्त उप सेदुर् आगन् ततो दीक्षाम् ऋषयः स्वर्विदः | ततः क्षत्रं बलम् ओजश् च जातं तद् अस्मै देवा अभि सं नमन्ताम् || धाता विधाता परमोत संदृक् प्रजापतिः परमेष्ठी सुवर्च्चाः | स्तोमांश् छन्दांसि निविदो म आहुर् एतस्मै राष्ट्रम् अभि सं नमन्ताम् || अभ्य् आ वर्तध्वम् उप सेवताग्निम् अयं शास्ताधिपतिर् नो अस्तु | अस्य विज्ञानम् अनु सं रभध्वम् इमं पश्चाद् अनु जीवाथ सर्वे || अलर्दो नाम जातो ऽसि पुरा सूर्यात् पुरोषसः | तं त्वा सपत्नक्षयणं वेदाथ विष्टम्भजम्भनम् || नार्धे प्रमीयेत तरेद् द्विषन्तं कल्पेत वाक्यं पृतनाः सहेत | प्रमायुकं तस्य द्विषन्तम् आहुर् इरामणिं बैल्वं यो बिभर्त्ति ||
12.4.e: With auspicious glances they have sat down. The E,sis who know heaven have come to the consecration. Then were heroism, strength, and might born. May this the gods to him make obedient. Creator, disposer, highest seer, Prajapati, the supreme, the splendid. The Stomas, the metres, the Nivids mine they call. To him may they make the kingdom obedient." Approach hither, pay him honour. Let Agni be our ruler and our king. Be ye in accordance with his will. On him hereafter do ye all depend. Thou art born, Alarda by name, before the sun, before the dawn. I know thee as destroyer of my enemies, and overthrower of their supports. He will not be cut off in the midst (of life), he will overcome his foe, he will be skilled in speech, he will be strong against battles, his foe they call likely to perish, who bears a comforting amulet of Bilva.
12.4.m:
Beholding the auspicious, the ṛṣis who found heaven approached and arrived at initiation; / from that were born dominion, strength, and power: to him let the gods bow down! ||16
Creator, dispenser, highest and all-seeing, Prajāpati, supreme, full of splendour— / the stoma praises, metres, and nivid formulas speak of me: to him let the realm bow down! ||17
Turn towards [him], wait upon Agni; may this ruler be our overlord! / Follow his understanding, start in unison; after him shall you all live! ||18
You are born by the name Alarda, before the sun, before the dawn; / as such I know you, the destroyer of rivals, the crusher of hindrances. ||19
He will not die halfway; he will cross over the hater, his speech will prevail, he will overcome hosts; / subject to death is the hater of him, they say, who wears the Irā-amulet of bilva wood. ||20

12.5.s: na sa śaptam aśnāti kilbiṣaṃ kṛtaṃ nainaṃ divyo varuṇo hanti bhītam | nainaṃ kruddhaṃ manyavo 'bhi yantīrāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti || nāsya tvacaṃ hiṃsati jātvedā na māṃsam aśnāti na hanti tāni | śatāyur asmiñ jaradaṣṭiḥ praitīrāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti || nāsya prajā duṣyati jāyamānā na śailago bhavati na pāpakṛtyā | nānyan mithas tasya kuleṣu jāyata irāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti || nāsyāpavādā na pravādakā gṛhe na saṃpatatryo na viveśa tasmai | nāsminn alakṣmīḥ kurute niveśanam irāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti || nainaṃ rakṣo na piśāco hinasti na jambhako nāpy asuro na yakṣaḥ | na sūtikā tasya kuleṣu jāyate irāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti ||
12.5.d: न स शप्तम् अश्नाति किल्बिषं कृतं नैनं दिव्यो वरुणो हन्ति भीतम् | नैनं क्रुद्धं मन्यवो ऽभि यन्तीरामणिं बैल्वं यो बिभर्त्ति || नास्य त्वचं हिंसति जात्वेदा न मांसम् अश्नाति न हन्ति तानि | शतायुर् अस्मिञ् जरदष्टिः प्रैतीरामणिं बैल्वं यो बिभर्त्ति || नास्य प्रजा दुष्यति जायमाना न शैलगो भवति न पापकृत्या | नान्यन् मिथस् तस्य कुलेषु जायत इरामणिं बैल्वं यो बिभर्त्ति || नास्यापवादा न प्रवादका गृहे न संपतत्र्यो न विवेश तस्मै | नास्मिन्न् अलक्ष्मीः कुरुते निवेशनम् इरामणिं बैल्वं यो बिभर्त्ति || नैनं रक्षो न पिशाचो हिनस्ति न जम्भको नाप्य् असुरो न यक्षः | न सूतिका तस्य कुलेषु जायते इरामणिं बैल्वं यो बिभर्त्ति ||
12.5.e: He eats not accursed food, he commits no sin, the heavenly Varuna terrifies him not, nor slays him, wrath overcomes him not in anger, who bears a comforting amulet of Bilva. Jatavedas injures not his skin. He eats not flesh nor harms these (creatures). After a hundred (years of life), reaching old age, in this world, he departs, who bears a comforting amulet of Bilva. No offspring of his is harmed in birth, no robber, no evil deed is there, nothing else amiss happens in his families, who bears a comforting amulet of Bilva. In his house there are no reviling nor scolding women, nor those who quarrel. Misfortune comes not to him, nor does she fix her abode in him, who bears a comforting amulet of Bilva. Him neither Raksas nor Pisiica injures, nor Jambhaka, nor Asura, nor Yaksa. In his house there is no lying-in woman, who bears a comforting amulet of Bilva.
12.5.m:
He does not suffer [from] a curse, nor from a sin committed; heavenly Varuṇa does not strike him when afraid; / rages do not overtake him in anger—he who wears the Irā-amulet of bilva wood. ||21
Jātavedas does not injure his skin, does not consume his flesh, does not slay those [limbs]; / living a hundred years, reaching old age, he departs—he who wears the Irā-amulet of bilva wood. ||22
His offspring born to him does not suffer, nor does he become rock-like, nor does evil sorcery [affect him]; / nothing amiss is born in his family—he who wears the Irā-amulet of bilva wood. ||23
In his house there are no detractors, no slanderers; swooping birds do not enter [his dwelling]; / misfortune makes no dwelling in him—he who wears the Irā-amulet of bilva wood. ||24
Neither a rakṣas nor a piśāca harms him, / nor a jambhaka demon, nor an asura, nor a yakṣa; / no child-bed spirit is born in his family—he who wears the Irā-amulet of bilva wood. ||25

12.6.s: nainaṃ vyāghro na vṛko na dvīpī na śvāpadaṃ hiṃsati kiṃcanainam | na hastinaṃ kruddham upaiti bhītim irāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti || nainaṃ sarpo na pṛdākur hinasti na vṛściko na tiraścīnarājiḥ | nainaṃ kṛṣṇo 'hir abhi saṃhata irāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti || nainaṃ pramattaṃ varuṇo hinasti na makaro na grahaḥ śiṃśumāraḥ | pārāvarāc chivam asmai kṛṇotīrāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti || pramāyukam asya dviṣantam āhuḥ | puṣpam iva chinnaṃ saha bandhanena | ogha iva śāpān pra ṇudāt sapatnān | irāmaṇiṃ bailvaṃ yo bibhartti || ayaṃ maṇiḥ pratisaro jāmbo jīvāya badhyate | anenendro vṛtram ahann ṛṣiṇā ca manīṣiṇā ||
12.6.d: नैनं व्याघ्रो न वृको न द्वीपी न श्वापदं हिंसति किंचनैनम् | न हस्तिनं क्रुद्धम् उपैति भीतिम् इरामणिं बैल्वं यो बिभर्त्ति || नैनं सर्पो न पृदाकुर् हिनस्ति न वृश्चिको न तिरश्चीनराजिः | नैनं कृष्णो ऽहिर् अभि संहत इरामणिं बैल्वं यो बिभर्त्ति || नैनं प्रमत्तं वरुणो हिनस्ति न मकरो न ग्रहः शिंशुमारः | पारावराच् छिवम् अस्मै कृणोतीरामणिं बैल्वं यो बिभर्त्ति || प्रमायुकम् अस्य द्विषन्तम् आहुः | पुष्पम् इव छिन्नं सह बन्धनेन | ओघ इव शापान् प्र णुदात् सपत्नान् | इरामणिं बैल्वं यो बिभर्त्ति || अयं मणिः प्रतिसरो जाम्बो जीवाय बध्यते | अनेनेन्द्रो वृत्रम् अहन्न् ऋषिणा च मनीषिणा ||
12.6.e: Him neither tiger, nor yolf, nor panther, nor beast of prey whatsoever hurts. No angry elej)hant meets he to scare him, who bears a comforting amulet of Bilva. No serpent, nor viper, nor scorpion, nor striped one, nor black one injures him, who bears a comforting amulet of Bilva. He sins not so that Varuna harms him; no crocodile, nor shark, nor porpoise injures him; on all sides it makes peace for him, who bears a comforting amulet of Bilva, They say his foe is likely to perish, like a flower fallen from its stalk. Like the flood pieces of wood, he shall overcome his foes, who bears a comforting amulet of Bilva. This amulet, the reverter, of the Jamba,'' is tied on for the sake of life. By it Indra slew Yrtra, and by the help of the wise Rsi.
12.6.m:
Neither tiger, nor wolf, nor leopard, nor any wild beast harms him; / he comes to no fear from an enraged elephant—he who wears the Irā-amulet of bilva wood. ||26
Neither snake nor adder harms him, nor scorpion, nor the cross-striped snake; / the black serpent does not coil upon him—he who wears the Irā-amulet of bilva wood. ||27
Varuṇa does not harm him when careless, nor sea monster, nor crocodile, nor dolphin; / from near and far it creates well-being for him—he who wears the Irā-amulet of bilva wood. ||28
Subject to death is his hater, they say, / like a flower cut off together with its stem; / as a flood [sweeps away] curses, let it drive away rivals— / he who wears the Irā-amulet of bilva wood. ||29
This amulet, a protective amulet, / made of jambu wood, is bound on for life; / with this Indra slew Vṛtra, and with the wise seer. ||30

12.7.s: sahendra dviṣataḥ sahasvārātīḥ sahasva pṛtanāyataḥ | nāga iva pūrvapādābhyām abhi tiṣṭha pṛtanyataḥ || āgād ayaṃ bailvo maṇiḥ sapatnakṣapaṇo vṛṣā | taṃ paśyanti kavayaḥ sarvavīrā yathā sapatnān samare saheyuḥ || anṛtaṃ me maṇau sūtram aśvināv api nahyatām | bailvaḥ sahasravīryo 'si mā te bhartā riṣam aham || ghṛtād ullupto madhumān payasvān dhanaṃjayo dharuṇo dhārayiṣṇuḥ | rujan sapatnān adharāṃś ca kṛṇvan ā roha māṃ mahate saubhagāya || prajāpate na tvad etāny anyo viśvā jatāni pari tā babhūva | yatkāmas te juhumas tan no astu vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇām || śāsa itthā mahāṃ asīti pañca ||
12.7.d: सहेन्द्र द्विषतः सहस्वारातीः सहस्व पृतनायतः | नाग इव पूर्वपादाभ्याम् अभि तिष्ठ पृतन्यतः || आगाद् अयं बैल्वो मणिः सपत्नक्षपणो वृषा | तं पश्यन्ति कवयः सर्ववीरा यथा सपत्नान् समरे सहेयुः || अनृतं मे मणौ सूत्रम् अश्विनाव् अपि नह्यताम् | बैल्वः सहस्रवीर्यो ऽसि मा ते भर्ता रिषम् अहम् || घृताद् उल्लुप्तो मधुमान् पयस्वान् धनंजयो धरुणो धारयिष्णुः | रुजन् सपत्नान् अधरांश् च कृण्वन् आ रोह मां महते सौभगाय || प्रजापते न त्वद् एतान्य् अन्यो विश्वा जतानि परि ता बभूव | यत्कामस् ते जुहुमस् तन् नो अस्तु वयं स्याम पतयो रयीणाम् || शास इत्था महां असीति पञ्च ||
12.7.e: Overcome, Indra, our foes, overcome our enemies, overcome the warriors; like an elephant (?) with its fore-feet, outmatch the warriors. Here has come the amulet of Bilva, the strong subduer of foes. The Rsis, all heroic, behold it that they may overcome their foes in the battle. Ambrosia is the thread in this amulet. May the Asvins fasten (the thread). Thou art of the Bilva, of a thousand powers. May I that bear thee never be injured. Snatched out of ghee, rich in honey and milk, winning wealth, bearing and supporting, destroying our foes and putting them down, mount upon me for great good fortune. None other than thou (Prajapati) doth encircle all these beings. That for which we long in sacrificing to thee, be that ours. May we be lords of riches. Then come five verses, (beginning), 'Thou art the great ruler here.'
12.7.m:
Overcome, O Indra, the haters; overcome the foes; overcome those who wage battle! / As an elephant with its front feet, trample upon those who fight! ||31
Hither has come this amulet of bilva wood, bull-like, destroyer of rivals; / the poets, whose heroes are whole, behold it, so that they may overcome their rivals in battle. ||32
Untwisted is the thread on my amulet; let the two Aśvins bind it fast! / Made of bilva wood, you possess a thousand potencies; may I, your bearer, suffer no harm! ||33
Smeared with clarified butter, full of honey, rich in milk, winning wealth, supporting, sustaining, / breaking rivals and casting them low: mount upon me for great good fortune! ||34
O Prajāpati, no other than you has encompassed all these creatures. / With whatever desire we offer to you, let that be ours; may we be lords of riches! ||35
[The hymn beginning] "Rule indeed, great thou art" consists of five verses.

12.8.s: athāto maṇikalpaḥ | bhūtikāmaḥ puṣpeṇa trirātropoṣito jīvato hastino dantān mātrām uddhṛtyāgnim upasamādhāya parisamuhya paristīrya paryukṣya dakṣiṇaṃ jānv ācyottarato 'gneḥ kaṃse maṇiṃ kṛtvā hutvā homān maṇau saṃpātam ānayet | hastivarcasam ity etābhiḥ pratyṛcam aṣṭābhiḥ saptarātraṃ madhusarpiṣor vāsayitvā trirātram ekāṃ vā badhnīyād ghṛtād ullupta ity etayarcā | ata evottaraṃ ṣaḍbhir hṛdayaśūlāgramaṇiṃ pratodāgramaṇiṃ vā muśalāgramaṇiṃ vā khadirasāramaṇiṃ vā māṃsaudane vāsayitvā trirātram ekāṃ vā badhnīyāt | ata evottaraṃ catasṛbhir vṛṣabhaśṛṅgāgramaṇiṃ ghṛtaudane vāsayitvā trirātram ekāṃ vā badhnīyāt | ata evottaraṃ ekayairaṇḍamaṇiṃ tilaudane vāsayitvā trirātram ekāṃ vā badhnīyāt | ata evottaraṃ ṣoḷaśabhir bailvaṃ saptarātraṃ madhusarpiṣor vāsayitvā trirātram ekāṃ vā badhnīyād ghṛtād ullupta ity etayarcā | ata evottaraṃ pañcabhir mahāvarāsyodohaṃ mudgaudane vāsayitvā trirātram ekāṃ vā badhnīyāc chaktau sati prathamaṃ hastichāyāyāṃ vaiyāghre vāpi carmaṇy āsīno vāpi juhuyād āsīno vāpi juhuyāt ||
12.8.d: अथातो मणिकल्पः | भूतिकामः पुष्पेण त्रिरात्रोपोषितो जीवतो हस्तिनो दन्तान् मात्राम् उद्धृत्याग्निम् उपसमाधाय परिसमुह्य परिस्तीर्य पर्युक्ष्य दक्षिणं जान्व् आच्योत्तरतो ऽग्नेः कंसे मणिं कृत्वा हुत्वा होमान् मणौ संपातम् आनयेत् | हस्तिवर्चसम् इत्य् एताभिः प्रत्यृचम् अष्टाभिः सप्तरात्रं मधुसर्पिषोर् वासयित्वा त्रिरात्रम् एकां वा बध्नीयाद् घृताद् उल्लुप्त इत्य् एतयर्चा | अत एवोत्तरं षड्भिर् हृदयशूलाग्रमणिं प्रतोदाग्रमणिं वा मुशलाग्रमणिं वा खदिरसारमणिं वा मांसौदने वासयित्वा त्रिरात्रम् एकां वा बध्नीयात् | अत एवोत्तरं चतसृभिर् वृषभशृङ्गाग्रमणिं घृतौदने वासयित्वा त्रिरात्रम् एकां वा बध्नीयात् | अत एवोत्तरं एकयैरण्डमणिं तिलौदने वासयित्वा त्रिरात्रम् एकां वा बध्नीयात् | अत एवोत्तरं षोऌअशभिर् बैल्वं सप्तरात्रं मधुसर्पिषोर् वासयित्वा त्रिरात्रम् एकां वा बध्नीयाद् घृताद् उल्लुप्त इत्य् एतयर्चा | अत एवोत्तरं पञ्चभिर् महावरास्योदोहं मुद्गौदने वासयित्वा त्रिरात्रम् एकां वा बध्नीयाच् छक्तौ सति प्रथमं हस्तिछायायां वैयाघ्रे वापि चर्मण्य् आसीनो वापि जुहुयाद् आसीनो वापि जुहुयात् ||
12.8.e: Then follows the ritual of the amulet. A man who desires prosperity should fast on flowers for three nights, then taking a piece from a living 'elephant's tusk, he should pile up the fire, sweep out (the place of sacrifice), scatter grass, sprinkle water around, and bending his right knee, place the amulet in a vessel to the north of the fire, sacrifice, and pour upon the amulet the remnant from the oblation, to the accompaniment of the eight verses (vv. 1-8), beginning Splendour of the elephant,' verse bv verse. Then for seven nio hts, or three nights, or one he should leave it to stand in honey and ghee and then put it on, with the verse (v. 7) 'Snatched out of ghee.' Then next with six (vv. 9-14) he should put on, having left it to stand for three nights or one in (a mess of) meat and boiled rice, an amulet of the point of the heart-spit or the point of the goad or the point of the mortar or of the core of the Acacia catechu. Then next with four verses (vv. 15-18) he should put on an amulet of the point of a bull's horn, having left it to stand for three nights or one in (a mess of) ghee and boiled rice. Then next with one verse (v. 19) he should put on an amulet of the castor-oil plant, having left it to stand for three nights or one in (a mess of) sesamum and boiled rice. Then next with sixteen verses (vv. 20-35) he should put on an amulet of Bilva, having left it to stand for seven nights or three or one in honey and ghee, fastening it with the verse (v. 34) 'Snatched out of ghee.' Then with the next five (w. 36-40) verses he should bind on a splinter of the Fkus infectoria which he has left to stand for three nights or one in a (mess of) beans and boiled rice. If possible he should first sacrifice in the shadow of an elephant or on a tiger's skin or sitting.
12.8.m: Now next, the rule for amulets. One who desires prosperity, having fasted for three nights under the constellation Puṣya, having taken a measure from the tusk of a living elephant, having built up the fire, swept around it, strewn it, sprinkled it, bending the right knee, having placed the amulet in a bronze vessel to the north of the fire, having offered the oblations, should pour the residue of the offering onto the amulet. Having kept it steeped in honey and clarified butter for seven nights, or for three nights, or for one [night], with these eight verses, verse by verse, beginning with ‘Elephant's splendour’ [hastivarcasam], one should bind it on with the verse ‘Drawn up from ghee’ [ghṛtād ulluptaḥ]. Following this, with six [verses], having kept an amulet from the tip of a spit for roasting the heart, or an amulet from the tip of a goad, or an amulet from the tip of a pestle, or an amulet of khadira-heartwood steeped in meat-rice for three nights or for one [night], one should bind it on. Following this, with four [verses], having kept an amulet from the tip of a bull's horn steeped in ghee-rice for three nights or for one [night], one should bind it on. Following this, with one [verse], having kept a castor amulet steeped in sesame-rice for three nights or for one [night], one should bind it on. Following this, with sixteen [verses], having kept a bilva amulet steeped in honey and clarified butter for seven nights, or for three nights, or for one [night], one should bind it on with the verse ‘Drawn up from ghee’. Following this, with five [verses], having kept the udder of a great wild sow steeped in mung-bean rice for three nights or for one [night], one should bind it on; if able, first in the shadow of an elephant or seated on a tiger skin he should offer, or seated he should offer.

13.1.s: athāto vairāgyasaṃskṛte śarīre brahmayajñaniṣṭho bhavet | apa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati | tad u ha vātmā draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavya iti | tam etaṃ vedānuvacanena vividiṣanti brahmacaryeṇa tapasā śraddhayā yajñenānāśakena ceti māṇḍūkeyaḥ | tasmād evaṃvic chānto dānta uparatas titikṣuḥ śraddhāvitto bhūtvātmany evātmānaṃ paśyed iti māṇḍavyaḥ | yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ puruṣaḥ prāṇeṣu sa eṣa neti nety ātmā na gṛhya idaṃ brahmedaṃ kṣatram ime devā ime vedā ime lokā imāni sarvāṇi bhūtānīdaṃ sarvaṃ yad ayam ātmā | sa eṣa tat tvam asīty ātmāvagamyo 'haṃ brahmāsmīti | tad etad brahmāpūrvam aparam anaparam anantaram abāhyam ayam ātmā brahma sarvānubhūr ity anuśāsanam iti yājñavalkyaḥ | tad etan nāputrāya nānantevāsine vā brūyād iti | ya imām adbhiḥ parigṛhītāṃ vasumatīṃ dhanasya pūrṇāṃ dadyād idam eva tato bhūya idam eva tato bhūya ity anuśāsanam | tām etām upaniṣadaṃ vedaśiro na yathā kathaṃ cana vadet | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam ||
13.1.d: अथातो वैराग्यसंस्कृते शरीरे ब्रह्मयज्ञनिष्ठो भवेत् | अप पुनर्मृत्युं जयति | तद् उ ह वात्मा द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यो मन्तव्यो निदिध्यासितव्य इति | तम् एतं वेदानुवचनेन विविदिषन्ति ब्रह्मचर्येण तपसा श्रद्धया यज्ञेनानाशकेन चेति माण्डूकेयः | तस्माद् एवंविच् छान्तो दान्त उपरतस् तितिक्षुः श्रद्धावित्तो भूत्वात्मन्य् एवात्मानं पश्येद् इति माण्डव्यः | यो ऽयं विज्ञानमयः पुरुषः प्राणेषु स एष नेति नेत्य् आत्मा न गृह्य इदं ब्रह्मेदं क्षत्रम् इमे देवा इमे वेदा इमे लोका इमानि सर्वाणि भूतानीदं सर्वं यद् अयम् आत्मा | स एष तत् त्वम् असीत्य् आत्मावगम्यो ऽहं ब्रह्मास्मीति | तद् एतद् ब्रह्मापूर्वम् अपरम् अनपरम् अनन्तरम् अबाह्यम् अयम् आत्मा ब्रह्म सर्वानुभूर् इत्य् अनुशासनम् इति याज्ञवल्क्यः | तद् एतन् नापुत्राय नानन्तेवासिने वा ब्रूयाद् इति | य इमाम् अद्भिः परिगृहीतां वसुमतीं धनस्य पूर्णां दद्याद् इदम् एव ततो भूय इदम् एव ततो भूय इत्य् अनुशासनम् | ताम् एताम् उपनिषदं वेदशिरो न यथा कथं चन वदेत् | तद् एतद् ऋचाभ्युदितम् ||
13.1.e: Then when his body has been made prepared for indifference to desire, he should be bent on the Brahman offering. So he drives repeated death away. 'The self is to be seen, to be heard, to be thought, to be meditated on,' 'Him they seek to know by repeating the Vedas, by studentship, hj asceticism, by faith, by sacrifice, by fasting,' says Mandukeya. Therefore, he who knows this, calm, restrained, still, enduring, becoming full of faith, should see the self in the self,' says Mandavya. '" The person among the breath composed of knowledge is incomprehensible, to be distinguished as 'No, no.' This self is the warrior-class, this the priesthood, this the gods, this the Vedas, this the worlds, this all beings, this is all. This is 'That art thou.' The self is to be recognised in 'I am Brahman.' This Brahman, without predecessor, without superior, without other, immediate, without an exterior, is this self, Brahman(n.), all-experiencing," such is the teaching,' says Yajnavalkya. 'That one should not proclaim to one who is not a son or a pupil.' 'Were a man to offer this earth surrounded by water and filled with wealth, yet is this more than that, more than that,' is the teaching. This Upaniṣad he should declare to be the head of the Veda in very truth. This is declared in a Re:—
13.1.m: Now, then, when the body is purified by dispassion, one should become devoted to the recitation of the Veda (brahmayajña). He wards off re-death. And so indeed: 'The self is to be seen, to be heard, to be reflected upon, to be meditated upon.' 'They seek to know him through the study of the Veda, through chaste studenthood (brahmacarya), through austerity, through faith, through sacrifice, and through fasting'—so says Māṇḍūkeya. 'Therefore, knowing thus, having become calm, controlled, tranquil, patient, and possessing faith, one should see the self in the self alone'—so says Māṇḍavya. 'That person here who consists of consciousness among the breaths, he is this self: not this, not that. It is ungraspable. This Brahman, this nobility, these deities, these Vedas, these worlds, all these beings, all this is what this self is.' 'That is to be understood as the self: "That thou art," "I am Brahman."' 'This Brahman is without before, without after, without inner, without outer; this self is Brahman, experiencing everything'—such is the instruction, so says Yājñavalkya. 'This one should not tell to one who is not a son, nor to one who is not a pupil.' 'Even if one should give this earth encircled by the waters and filled with wealth, this alone is greater than that, this alone is greater than that'—such is the instruction. This secret teaching (upaniṣad), the head of the Veda, one must not speak at random. This has been expressed in a verse:

14.1.s: ṛcāṃ mūrdhānaṃ yajuṣām uttamāṅgam | sāmnāṃ śiro 'tharvāṇāṃ muṇḍamuṇḍam | nādhīte 'dhīte vedam āhus tam ajñam | śiraś chitvāsau kurute kabandham ||
14.1.d: ऋचां मूर्धानं यजुषाम् उत्तमाङ्गम् | साम्नां शिरो ऽथर्वाणां मुण्डमुण्डम् | नाधीते ऽधीते वेदम् आहुस् तम् अज्ञम् | शिरश् छित्वासौ कुरुते कबन्धम् ||
14.1.e: Head of the Re verses, highest member of the Yajus verses, pinnacle of the Samans, the supreme tonsure of the Atharvans, he who studies not the Yeda, him they call ignorant. Cleaving his head, he makes himself a corpse.
14.1.m: The head of the Ṛgveda verses, the highest limb of the Yajurveda formulas, / the head of the Sāmaveda melodies, the shaved crown of the Atharvaveda texts: / he who studies the Veda without studying [this], they call him ignorant; / cutting off the head, he makes a headless trunk.

14.2.s: sthāṇur ayaṃ bhārahāraḥ kilābhūt | adhītya vedaṃ na vijānāti yo 'rtham | yo 'rthajña it sakalaṃ bhadram aśnute | nākam eti jñānavidhūtapāpmā ||
14.2.d: स्थाणुर् अयं भारहारः किलाभूत् | अधीत्य वेदं न विजानाति यो ऽर्थम् | यो ऽर्थज्ञ इत् सकलं भद्रम् अश्नुते | नाकम् एति ज्ञानविधूतपाप्मा ||
14.2.e: He is but a pillar indeed who bears a burden, who repeats the Veda without knowing the meaning. Who knows the meaning alone wins prosperity. He goes to heaven, shaking off sin through knowledge.'
14.2.m: He is indeed a post, a mere bearer of a burden, / who, having studied the Veda, does not understand the meaning. / But he who knows the meaning attains all good; / shaking off evil through knowledge, he goes to heaven.

15.1.s: atha vaṃśaḥ | oṃ namo brahmaṇe nama ācāryebhyaḥ | guṇākhyāc chāṅkhāyanād asmābhir adhītam | guṇākhyaś śāṅkhāyanaḥ kahoḷāt kauṣītakeḥ | kahoḷaḥ kauṣītakir uddālakād āruṇeḥ | uddālaka āruṇiḥ priyavratāt saumāpeḥ | priyavrataḥ saumāpiḥ somapāt | somapaḥ saumāt prātiveśyāt | saumaḥ prātiveśyaḥ prativeśyāt | prativeśyo bṛhaddivāt | bṛhaddivaḥ sumnayoḥ | sumnayur uddālakāt | uddālako viśvamanasaḥ | viśvamanā vyaśvāt | vyaśvaḥ sākamaśvāt | sākamaśvo devarātāt | devarāto viśvāmitrāt | viśvāmitra indrāt | indraḥ prajāpateḥ | prajāpatir brahmaṇaḥ | brahmā svayaṃbhūḥ | namo brahmaṇe namo brahmaṇe ||
15.1.d: अथ वंशः | ओं नमो ब्रह्मणे नम आचार्येभ्यः | गुणाख्याच् छाङ्खायनाद् अस्माभिर् अधीतम् | गुणाख्यश् शाङ्खायनः कहोऌआत् कौषीतकेः | कहोऌअः कौषीतकिर् उद्दालकाद् आरुणेः | उद्दालक आरुणिः प्रियव्रतात् सौमापेः | प्रियव्रतः सौमापिः सोमपात् | सोमपः सौमात् प्रातिवेश्यात् | सौमः प्रातिवेश्यः प्रतिवेश्यात् | प्रतिवेश्यो बृहद्दिवात् | बृहद्दिवः सुम्नयोः | सुम्नयुर् उद्दालकात् | उद्दालको विश्वमनसः | विश्वमना व्यश्वात् | व्यश्वः साकमश्वात् | साकमश्वो देवरातात् | देवरातो विश्वामित्रात् | विश्वामित्र इन्द्रात् | इन्द्रः प्रजापतेः | प्रजापतिर् ब्रह्मणः | ब्रह्मा स्वयंभूः | नमो ब्रह्मणे नमो ब्रह्मणे ||
15.1.e: Om. Then follows the line of teachers. Honour to Brahman, honour to the teachers! We have learnt it from Gunakhya Siinkhayana, Gunakhya Sahkhiiyana from Kahola Kausitaki, Kahola KausTtaki from Uddalaka Aruni, Uddiilaka Aruni from Priyavrata Saumapi, Priyavrata Saumapi • from Somapa, Somapa from Soma - Prativesya, Soma Priitivesya from Prativesya, Prativesya from Brhaddiva, Brhaddiva from Sumnayu, Sumnayu from Uddalaka, Uddalaka from Visvamanas, Visvamanas from Vyasva, Vj asva from Sakamasva Devarata, Devarata from Viśvāmitra, VisvJimitra from Indra, Indra from Prajapati, PrajcTjDati from Brahman, Brahman(n.) is self-existent. Honour to Brahman, honour to Brahman!
15.1.m: Now, the lineage of teachers (vaṃśa). Om, homage to Brahman! Homage to the teachers! We have studied [this] from Guṇākhya Śāṅkhāyana; Guṇākhya Śāṅkhāyana from Kahola Kauṣītaki; Kahola Kauṣītaki from Uddālaka Āruṇi; Uddālaka Āruṇi from Priyavrata Saumāpi; Priyavrata Saumāpi from Somapa; Somapa from Sauma Prātiveśya; Sauma Prātiveśya from Prativeśya; Prativeśya from Bṛhaddiva; Bṛhaddiva from Sumnayu; Sumnayu from Uddālaka; Uddālaka from Viśvamanas; Viśvamanas from Vyaśva; Vyaśva from Sākamaśva; Sākamaśva from Devarāta; Devarāta from Viśvāmitra; Viśvāmitra from Indra; Indra from Prajāpati; Prajāpati from Brahman; Brahman is Svayambhū. Homage to Brahman! Homage to Brahman!
